findings.claim: Pending delivery is still not a live invariant. The new allocation rule can erase an undelivered heartbeat-gap event, and reconciliation has a permanent history-size failure mode that can strand any warning or recovery despite healthy later HTTP responses.

manifestations.claim: After W2/W3 persist a nhip_tim_gian_doan event, a crash before W5 or a definite failed POST leaves cho_bao pending. At the next healthy iteration S/F/reason and the last acknowledged green state are unchanged, but the new heartbeat is moi. Rules (a)-(c) select no event and allocation clears cho_bao. Deviation 10 discusses changed states; no state changed in this trace. The claims at the objective, section 10 and I6 that the next healthy iteration delivers it are false.

D14 always scans all comments from page 1 and must finish within 10 pages of 100. Once the single long-lived Issue has 1001 comments, the first pending event after any failed POST/readback can never reconcile: every subsequent iteration sees rel=next, locks sending, retains cho_bao, and returns 3. There is no bounded-history checkpoint, narrowed search or recovery procedure for this condition. This affects warning, recovery and gap events.

evidence.observed_output: pending-heartbeat-gap: durable id=100-1; next heartbeat=moi; next_POST=0; pending_after=null; delivered_comments=0. Controls pending-warning and pending-recovery retry id=100-1 once; acknowledged controls issue zero POSTs.
D14-history-cap: 1000 comments -> 10 pages, complete; 1001 and 1002 -> 11 pages, incomplete, POST=0, pending unchanged, rc=3.
The per-Issue endpoint orders by ascending ID, supports since (last-updated timestamp), and caps per_page at 100. No server-side event-id filter is documented.

findings.claim: Sorting fixes the original API-order counterexample, but the replacement all-or-nothing deadline is not enforced at completion. The concrete algorithm checks before physical calls only and does not clamp a call to remaining phase time or check after the final call/CPU work. Thus a successful result can escape after the frozen budget, contrary to S1 and the stated budget proof.

manifestations.claim: Final T7 starts at monotonic elapsed 599s and succeeds after 2s, within HAN_GOI=30. There is no next evaluation call at which the prescribed precheck notices 601>600. The specified loop can publish fresh and advance dong_den after budget exhaustion.

Parsing/decompression after a completed HTTP call is also outside the explicitly listed budget checkpoints. timeout-minutes:20 is an external cancellation, not a substitute for completing heartbeat/error reporting under the 600+180 contract.

findings.claim: The reader now validates values, but the writer/input domain is not closed under those validations. Valid executions can be required to write a heartbeat that the same spec requires the next iteration to reject, losing acknowledgement and obligation state.

manifestations.claim: Before the first required cron frame, dong_den has an empty legal range. B1a may merge Monday, giving KHUNG_DAU on the following Saturday; B2 may activate that Monday. Initial dong_den=KHUNG_DAU-7d, while reader maximum=khung(T)-7d=KHUNG_DAU-14d. No value satisfies both bounds; there is no activation wait or pre-start representation.

The catch-all requires raw module.qualname diagnostic codes, including danh_gia_nem, but heartbeat ma_ly_do must be ASCII and <=200 characters. Python permits Unicode/long exception class names. Those allowed exceptions yield mandated codes outside the heartbeat domain; ensure_ascii escapes JSON serialization but does not change the parsed string.

run_id/run_attempt and accepted B2_RUN_* context have only a positive-integer lower bound, whereas event id limits the decimal components to 20/10 digits. Accepted context run_id=10**20 produces a 21-digit id that cho_bao/da_bao must reject. This is a domain inconsistency, not a claim that GitHub currently emits such IDs.

findings.claim: TRAN_GOI limits downloaded compressed bytes only. The mandated doc_zip primitive opens and reads every file before cardinality/schema checks, with no expanded-byte/member limit or interruptible parse budget. A small accepted download can allocate far beyond 50MiB and prevent the heartbeat write phase; catch Exception cannot guarantee recovery from process termination.

manifestations.claim: This applies to both T2 receipt ZIPs and every T5 evidence ZIP. The safe real probe compresses 8388608 bytes into 8296 bytes (1011.2x), well below TRAN_GOI. No constraint in the candidate bounds the subsequent expansion or accumulated decompressed content. The 20-minute job cap can cancel the process, but cannot produce the promised reported unknown and heartbeat.

evidence.observed_output: zip-expansion: compressed=8296; expanded=8388608; under_TRAN_GOI=true; ratio=1011.2. Only an 8MiB probe was allocated; no OOM or runner-kill claim is made.

suggested_fix.where: ops/specs/wp1494-r1/SPEC.md section 3 doc_zip/byte-budget contract and T2/T5 acceptance; the limit must act before allocation, not after consumer validation.
suggested_fix.how: Define and justify limits for expanded bytes, member count and cumulative retained data. Read bounded chunks under the remaining deadline; classify resource exhaustion as unmeasured rather than corrupt observed bytes. Measure representative B1 artifacts before freezing thresholds and retain a separate write allowance.
suggested_fix.locking_test: Use the bounded ZIP fixture in python3 -B /tmp/wp1494-review-r2/probes.py at an injectable small expansion limit, with below/at/above controls for T2 and T5. Verify refusal occurs before reading the excess bytes and that heartbeat reporting still executes. Mutants removing expanded-size or cumulative-size guards must die through their designated case class.
suggested_fix.what_fix_may_spawn: Overly small limits reject valid audits; checking only ZIP metadata trusts forged sizes; reclassifying resource refusal as invalid content can misreport an infrastructure limitation as an audit failure.
